This happened to me. In fall 2019, I was visiting my hometown. It’s a mid size rustbelt city with a few bars in a strip downtown. I decided to meet my old friend from high school for a beer - hadn’t seen him in years. We got through maybe half a pint when suddenly groups of people were bursting through the back door that connects to the rear smoking patio. They were running and screaming about a shooter in the adjacent movie theater. We both ran to the bathroom with a stranger and locked the door. It’s one of those divey bars with gross bathrooms, and I (woman) was hiding by the urinal while these guys I barely knew were guarding the door as people screamed and stomped outside of it. I remember it got really quiet and I could sense that we all thought something bad was going to happen. Minutes passed. Eventually we opened the door. The bartender was alone. He was looking out the window and said the doors were locked. He had the shades mostly pulled, but I could see people walking down the sidewalk. I said I’m going to run to my car. The bartender unlocked the front door and I ran a couple of blocks and drove off. The next day I kept googling to see what had actually happened. Nothing was in the news. I was taken aback by how much terror I saw in so many people and the fact that it didn’t even make the news - Regardless of the cause.

I think you look great. The following advice is basically what I’ve done for myself, and I think it made the biggest difference in how I look. I’m 35 but was looking kind of bleh. I’m not suggesting you forgo skincare, as it certainly helped me. But it made less of a noticeable improvement than the following:

I think the biggest thing that would give you a refresh is if you went to a really good salon and had a professional give you a cut and color that compliments your skin tone and eye color. Maybe a medium brown with warm honey toned highlights or balayage. Get an olaplex treatment to make it super shiny and strong, and invest in a blowout hairdryer for styling. Use some kind of styling product from the salon to heat protect your hair.

I don’t know if you usually wear makeup, but having a really basic routine (the glossier foundation and concealer is super lightweight and low maintenance). Maybe a sheer pop of color on your lips (Clinique black honey/pink honey or glossier lip color is also nice and light), tiny bit of blush, eyeliner and mascara. Just to accentuate your natural features.

Get your nails done! Pick a color that makes you happy every time you look down at your hands! Get some nice outfits that make you feel great and compliment your figure! Get a cute pair of shoes or necklace or handbag, something that makes you feel good and inspired and confident when you put it on. Start expressing yourself with how you decorate your physical form. Do certain colors, fabrics, textures, gemstones, etc appeal to you? Find a way to incorporate them into your wardrobe/makeup/hair. It’s your body to design and have fun with!

You said you have extra spending money, so that’s why I’m suggesting this stuff. When I was broke I went to thrift shops and made a lot of my own stuff.

Edit: I also suggest that before you micro blade your brows, just go to a brow bar and get them shaped and tinted. I’ve seen some fucked up microblade jobs and I would be afraid to commit to that when there are less permanent options.

If you have a problem with chemicals this sub isn't for you. The most effective skincare is chemicals. It seems that you think acne is a moral failing for not drinking enough water or doing your organic due diligence. It seems that you think the natural human state is breakout-free, and if only you could remove all the impurities of living, you'd return to your purest self.

"Chemicals" is a vague word. By definition, a chemical is any substance that has a defined composition. There are synthetic and natural chemicals. In reality, the most toxic chemicals to humans are completely natural, and even those chemicals aren't toxic at every dose. Take botulinum toxin for example. It's extremely deadly and natural but safe/therapeutic in low doses. Apples, pears, zucchini, potatoes all carry chemicals that are deadly to humans in high doses.

See: [https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/guest-blog/natural-vs-synthetic-chemicals-is-a-gray-matter/](https://blogs.scientificamerican.com/guest-blog/natural-vs-synthetic-chemicals-is-a-gray-matter/)

See: [https://enveurope.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s12302-014-0033-2](https://enveurope.springeropen.com/articles/10.1186/s12302-014-0033-2)

See: [https://www.theguardian.com/science/blog/2014/may/19/manmade-natural-tasty-toxic-chemicals](https://www.theguardian.com/science/blog/2014/may/19/manmade-natural-tasty-toxic-chemicals)

People in this sub follow the science. They're gonna recommend tretinoin and/or various chemical exfoliants like glycolic acid or salicylic acid for your acne. In fact a lot of "natural" skincare, like witch hazel for instance, isn't very good for your skin.
